newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe money rates softer as liquidity improves.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe money rates softer as liquidity improves.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted softer on Tuesday, dealers said.
They added that most market players were looking to stock up on 91-day central bank paper before Thursday's weekly auction, which was likely to see rates lowered.
"Everyone wants to buy treasury bills now so they can sell them at a lower rate after Thursday and make a profit," one dealer said.
On Tuesday, discount houses were buying treasury bills from the Reserve Bank at a steady 21.46 percent but were selling them softer at 21.25 percent, down from Monday's 21.35 percent.
NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 23.25 percent from 23.50 but their selling rate remained steady at 22.50.
Bankers acceptance bills were at 21.75 and 21.50 percent from 22 and 21.50 percent while call money was stable at 23 percent.
The central Reserve Bank indicated a market surplus of Z$101 million at the start of business, up from Monday's Z$38 million.
